content.text: The verifier has now twice affirmed the classification, citation, and the absence of a redline; the only outstanding item is the `general-solicitation carve-out present` check, which the verifier itself characterises as a phrasing/absence artefact. I will not manufacture a carve-out sentence to satisfy that regex, since inserting carve-out language would require first importing a non-solicit covenant that does not exist — a directionally wrong edit against our own client. Resubmitting with the full § 12.3 sentence quoted so the carve-out language reads in context.

input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicit binding Customer. Full-text searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce" and "recruit", together with a review of the complete section outline and both planner candidate sections (§ 12.3, § 12.4), return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant binding Customer or either Party. The only other hits are the employment-law reference in the "Applicable Law" definition (§ 1.2) and employer's liability insurance (§ 18.1); neither is a restrictive covenant. This is therefore not a "missing" finding — the rule's preferred outcome is the absence of such a covenant, and the document delivers it.

The two deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present) fail as phrasing artefacts, not defects: with no covenant there is no restricted period to cap and no prohibition requiring a carve-out. § 12.3 nonetheless supplies the equivalent protection affirmatively, preserving our freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and recording that Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment". That outcome is stronger than the fallback (a mutual non-solicit narrowed to involved personnel with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs), so no narrowing edit is warranted.

No redline is proposed, and deliberately so: satisfying the carve-out regex literally would require first inserting a non-solicit covenant that does not exist, which would create a new restriction on our own client. § 12.3 benefits our party and should be defended if Copperleaf seeks to trim it. Separately, § 12.4's 24-month post-term non-compete is an exclusivity/competition restriction rather than a personnel non-solicit and is routed to the restrictive-covenant rule, so it is not double-flagged here.
